1.explanation: We use ESLint’s Node API (CLIEngine) to simulate the exact configuration from the bug report (babel-eslint parser + constructor-super rule). The code string includes a derived ES6 class with a try/catch around a for–of loop immediately after super(). When CLIEngine parses and runs constructor-super on this text, it throws the internal “superCalled” error and/or reports a bogus parsing error on the blank line. To observe the failure, save this script as repro.js, install eslint and babel-eslint locally, and run node repro.js.
1.bug_scenario: In a derived ES6 class constructor that calls super(), wrapping a for–of loop inside a try/catch block causes the ESLint “constructor-super” rule to crash. In our test (using babel-eslint + "react-app" config), editing a trailing blank line or adding/removing code after the try/catch produces a “Cannot read property 'superCalled' of undefined” internal error and a spurious “Parsing error: Unexpected token” pointing at the blank line. This happens even though the code is syntactically valid and super() is called exactly once.
